html:
Sofala was a trading port on the coast of central Mozambique, the southernmost of the Swahili towns, through which gold and ivory from the Zimbabwe plateau went out to the Indian Ocean from about the 10th century.

Merchants from Kilwa, which controlled the port at its height, bought gold brought down from Great Zimbabwe and later Mutapa in exchange for cloth and beads. The gold made Kilwa rich.

The Portuguese built a fort at Sofala in 1505 to seize the trade, but traders moved to other routes, up the Zambezi. The harbour silted up, and the town declined, its role taken by the Island of Mozambique and later Beira nearby.
sum: Sofala was a trading port on the coast of central Mozambique, the southernmost of the Swahili towns, through which gold and ivory from the Zimbabwe plateau went out to the Indian Ocean from about the 10th century.
